scope: CA-P-2713 references and Atom lifecycle; no native source edit

candidates.kind: ordinary Markdown content, not a registered Property or Relation
candidates.depends_on: I admission is settled; root integrates this content into the standard Claim shape.
candidates.exact_proposed_text:
#### Code references

A Code Synopsis faithfully describes the context and state of the actual code at one or more ordinary Markdown-link code locations. Each link is unambiguous in its Project context. When an applicable Project.Settings.Code-Root Locator is declared, the link is resolved against it. A link may include an anchor, and an observed content digest may be recorded when a particular observation needs to be pinned.

Code references are ordinary Claim text, not a registered Property, Atom relation, Carrier replacement, or Journal implementation binding. They do not require a specification, a commit SHA, Git metadata, a snapshot status, locator grammar, or one-to-one source coverage.

The referenced code remains the truth of actual implementation. A difference from the synopsis or from an optional specification is neutral until assessment identifies a matter requiring resolution as a Concern.
fit: CA-R-2173 keeps logical artifacts distinct from their Carriers and permits directly edited Implementation to be authoritative for actual implementation.
CA-R-1978 already admits an optional Project.Settings.Code-Root Locator; this proposal uses it only when declared and requires no new root, locator grammar, or discovery procedure.
CA-R-1695 reserves stable locator plus digest for Journal implementation bindings, so this contract deliberately does not create such a binding.
not_proposed: No Code Reference Property or Atom, new Relation, carrier identity, commit-SHA field, Git dependency, snapshot status, source-coverage rule, or forced specification link.

candidates.kind: authoring guidance using declared relations only
candidates.exact_proposed_text:
An optional relationship is authored only when its declared meaning is true. A Code Synopsis may use CONTRIBUTES_TO toward a related specification, Analysis & Advisory Atom, or Task when the synopsis actually contributes toward that target; contribution does not assert satisfaction. An Analysis & Advisory Rationale that explains a Code Synopsis uses rationale_for from the Rationale to the synopsis. A Concern uses concern_about only after assessment identifies a matter requiring resolution, and targets the governed entity concerned.

implementation_of remains a relation from a governed Implementation Carrier to the specification Atom it implements; it is not a Code Synopsis-to-code or Code Synopsis-to-specification reference. evidence_for remains an evidence-Carrier relation and is not a replacement for Code References. No such optional relationship is required merely because a Code Synopsis exists.

candidates.exact_proposed_text:
A Code Synopsis is an Atom. It reuses the ordinary Atom identity, Status, Version, Updated At, and archival contracts. A code change at a referenced locator does not itself create a Code Synopsis successor or change its Status, Version, or Updated At. When an accepted edit of the synopsis is made, its ordinary Atom lifecycle applies.

Archiving a Code Synopsis preserves its Version and Updated At and does not create a version solely for archival.
fit: CA-R-1412, CA-R-1415, CA-R-1788, and CA-R-2565 already provide the applicable lifecycle constraints.
CA-R-2173 and CA-R-1873 establish the actual-implementation authority boundary; an authored synopsis remains an observation about that boundary rather than an automatic mirror of file state.
not_proposed: No new lifecycle status, automatic code-to-Atom synchronization, status transition, or Git-triggered update.
